Pathology

/puh-THOL-uh-jee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pathology means a deviation from a normal, healthy condition; the study of disease.

The biopsy went to the hospital's pathology department, where specialists would examine the cells for any sign of disease.

Worked Example

The orchard's oldest apple tree was dropping leaves in June, so Ms. Vance mailed a branch sample to the state agricultural lab. Two weeks later the report arrived, describing the pathology in detail: a fungal infection was blocking the tree's water-carrying vessels. What looked like simple thirst was actually a disease process — a true departure from the tree's healthy condition.

The lab report identifies the disease process disrupting the tree's normal, healthy functioning — that disease process is the pathology.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

disease: an unhealthy condition of the body

disorder: a disturbance of normal functioning

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

health: a normal, sound condition

wellness: the state of being in good health

Where it sits · how unhealthy the condition has become — abnormality → pathology → disease

abnormality vs. pathology: An abnormality is any departure from the usual, while a pathology is specifically an unhealthy one.

disease vs. pathology: A full-blown disease is a pathology at its most developed — actively damaging the body.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — patho-

Root — patho-: suffering, disease (Greek pathos)

Suffix — -logy

Suffix — -logy: the study of (Greek logos, 'word, reasoning')

Put it together

Put it together: Pathology pairs Greek pathos, 'suffering, disease,' with -logy, 'the study of.' The suffering root also builds sympathy ('suffering with'), empathy, and pathetic. Pathway is a false friend: the everyday word path is Old English and has nothing to do with Greek pathos.

Use the root in a new word: sympathy

Use the root in a new word: sympathy: Sympathy is literally 'suffering with' someone — Greek pathos, 'suffering,' the same root that opens pathology.

Word Choice

medical, scientific

Pathology is a clinical noun for disease itself or for the study of it. Keep it in its own lane within this unit: hazardous describes risky situations before harm occurs, and devastated describes the state of being overwhelmed once destruction has struck — pathology names the disease process itself.
